exposure: antepartum hemorrhage (APH) etiology (abnormal placental locations, abruptio placentae, other causes)
associated risk factors (anemia, hemorrhagic shock, DIC, ARF, morbidly adherent placenta)
cohort: The study included all patients admitted with a diagnosis of antepartum hemorrhage (APH) at a tertiary care hospital in North India over a one-year period.
finding: The institutional prevalence rate of APH was 7.5%, primarily due to abnormal placental locations (53.6%) and abruptio placentae (46%), leading to significant maternal and fetal morbidity and mortality.
mod_finding: Emergency primary lower segment Cesarean section (LSCS) was identified as the commonest and statistically significant mode of delivery for APH cases.
gest_age: Mean 34.3 +/- 2.3 weeks at termination of pregnancy
